text:
jana: Heads-up, the nightjar-int8 canary (on dedicated canary pool) is showing a 4x increase in structured-output parse failures for funcalls over the last hour. Mostly truncated JSON suffixes and occasional trailing-comma noise. :eyes:

mike: Yikes. This is the first int8 canary for nightjar, right? How does fp16 look on the same prompt set?

jana: Yes first int8 run. FP16 baseline is fine (parse fail ~0.4%), nightjar-int8 is ~2.1%. Sample logs:```INVOKE 1746503209 model=nightjar-int8 canary=42 prompt_id=abc123 status=200 tokens=342 out_trunc_suffix=true output_tail=... ,"action": "open_file",
  "path": "/etc/passwd"}```

ramon: That log smells like a suffix cutoff from KV-prefix batching + tokenization shift after quantization. We saw something similar with a different model when kvcache prefix length changed.

sasha: Can you repro locally with the exact canary config? If it's KVCACHE-related, disable continuous batching for a mirror and see if failure rate drops.

jana: Repro script I used (quick):```curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/invoke -d '{"model":"nightjar-int8","prompt":"<toolcall test>","max_tokens":512}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer x'``` Running 2000 samples against the canary pool produced the delta above.

eva: Quick mitigation: 1) reduce canary traffic to 10% and add a mirror to fp16 for divergence alerting, 2) run tokenization diff between fp16 vs int8 on the same prompts, 3) gate funcall responses with a soft-parse fallback (attempt JSON repair + single retry) to reduce customer impact.

mike: For the tokenization diff, run:```python -c "from tokenizers import Tokenizer; t=Tokenizer.from_file('nightjar-vocab.json'); a=t.encode('prompt'); print(a.ids)"``` Compare ids for quant vs fp16 vocab. If id shift is tiny that's weird.

ramon: Also check kernel-level EOS handling in int8 runtime path — we had a micro-optimization that elides an EOS sentinel on odd seq-lens. Could truncate suffix when sequences near batching boundary.

jana: I'm going to: (a) spin mirror fp16 replay, (b) disable continuous batching on canary pool for 1h, (c) add a soft-parse retry (1 retry) in the canary route. Will post numbers in ~30m.

deploy-bot: Canary nightsparrow-int8 -> nightjar-int8 rolled to 25% at 1746503000, monitor: https://deploys.redwood/invocations/1746503000

sasha: Thanks. If the retry + mirror drop failure below 0.8% we can proceed with more analysis offline. If not, hold the int8 rollout and start a bisect comparing quantization recipe diffs. :+1:

jana: Update (30m): disabling continuous batching dropped parse-fail to 0.9% on 2000 samples. Adding single JSON-repair retry drops to 0.45%. Looks like batching interaction is the main contributor.

mike: Great signal. Next steps: add an onboard check that runs tokenization and kvcache-boundary simulation for any int8 canary, and add a canary policy tweak to disable CB for initial 24h or until a boundary check passes automatically.

ramon: I'll file a short eng-ml incident note with the kvcache/batch interaction trace and link to the microkernel patch we should test.

jana: Filing now. Thanks all. :heart:
